text: MCX lists gold in five sizes. Their prices never line up, and traders keep asking: is that gap free money?
Most of the gap is the rulebook: purity, quote units, settlement city and expiry. AuLens converts every price to rupees per ten grams.
Our control pair, Gold Ten against Gold Guinea, must settle at zero. On all eighteen expiries, it lands within one rupee.
But the gap often widens in the final week, and closes only after a trader must exit for delivery.
We test it walk-forward: past data only, next-day fills, every cost included. The verdict: no edge.
Sixty-two trades, minus seventeen thousand rupees. It breaks even at under three rupees of slippage, about two ticks.
Every result is split by regime, including the April SEBI change and the May duty hike.
Six pairs in gold and silver, including two carry pairs across expiries, come back the same: no edge.
The curve also shows what holding gold costs: about six percent a year through 2025, nearly fourteen since the rally.
So AuLens stays quiet. It alerts only when a pair earns an edge and clears its costs.
AuLens. Gold and silver, six pairs, one honest verdict. Open source, and live today.
